 A look at the latest NBA Cup standings and how the NBA Cup bracket would look if group stage ended Friday night. Tom Dierberger | Share on Facebook Share on X Add us as a preferred source Stephon Castle, Dylan Harper and the Spurs routed the Warriors 123–85 at Frost Bank Center on Friday night. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect In this story:
 Atlanta Hawks Boston Celtics Brooklyn Nets Charlotte Hornets Chicago Bulls Cleveland Cavaliers Dallas Mavericks Denver Nuggets Detroit Pistons Golden State Warriors Houston Rockets Indiana Pacers Los Angeles Clippers Los Angeles Lakers Memphis Grizzlies Miami Heat Milwaukee Bucks Minnesota Timberwolves New Orleans Pelicans New York Knicks Oklahoma City Thunder Orlando Magic Philadelphia 76ers Phoenix Suns Portland Trail Blazers Sacramento Kings San Antonio Spurs Toronto Raptors Utah Jazz Washington Wizards Three weeks into the fourth edition of the NBA Cup, teams are starting to separate themselves from the pack—for better or worse. 
--> Three weeks into the fourth edition of the NBA Cup, teams are starting to separate themselves from the pack—for better or worse. 
 We witnessed a few ugly blowouts on Friday night. Without Steph Curry , the Warriors fell behind the Spurs 18–0 a few minutes into the first quarter and limped to a 123–85 loss. The Grizzlies beat the struggling Pelicans 142–111, and the Trail Blazers stayed hot with a 120–107 win over the Kings.
--> We witnessed a few ugly blowouts on Friday night. Without Steph Curry , the Warriors fell behind the Spurs 18–0 a few minutes into the first quarter and limped to a 123–85 loss. The Grizzlies beat the struggling Pelicans 142–111, and the Trail Blazers stayed hot with a 120–107 win over the Kings.
 The best game of the night was a back-and-forth affair between the Clippers and the Thunder. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander went off for 40 points, but Brook Lopez was clutch down the stretch and Los Angeles finished off Oklahoma City for a 113–112 upset win. This is March? Nay, this is the Cup.

 Over in the East, the Celtics remain the projected No. 1 seed. Boston didn’t play Friday night, but the Celtics are sitting pretty with a +53 point differential. Giannis Antetokounmpo and the Heat are off to a slow start this season, but you wouldn’t know it looking at the NBA Cup standings. Miami is a perfect 2–0 with matchups against the 76ers and Knicks to go. With an eight-point win over the Bucks, the Magic grab the No. 3 seed atop East Group A, and the Pistons sneak in as the wild card at 1–0.

 In the West, Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs hold a comfortable lead for the No. 1 seed after beating the Warriors by 38 points on Friday. San Antonio’s point differential in the NBA Cup is tied with Boston for the league high at +53. The Wolves, Mavs and Nuggets round out the field.
